_comment: Fleet provider registry. Copy to ./.fleet/providers.json (project) or ~/.fleet/providers.json (user) and edit to match what YOU actually have access to. Run /fleet-init to have Claude draft this for you with current models and pricing. Fields: enabled, adapter (codex|antigravity|gemini|opencode|claude|grok|cursor|copilot|qwen|droid|amp), access (subscription|api|local|free), default_model (REQUIRED for opencode, provider/model form; empty elsewhere = CLI default), max_workers, cost, strengths/weaknesses (short, honest, yours — these steer routing), context_window, trust (standard|restricted), notes. Optional per-provider: soft_weekly_cap {tasks and/or tokens} for quota pacing, review_after (ISO date) for scheduled access-term changes. Optional top-level supervisor block: the supervisor's OWN model rates, used for pre-dispatch spend ballparks and realized-savings estimates.

supervisor.notes: PLACEHOLDER — research the supervisor model's current API list price (web search, never memory) and date-stamp it, e.g. 'pricing verified 2026-08'. On a flat-rate plan, use the API list price for the same model — the market value of quota that delegation preserves. Cache rates are optional (self_usage.py assumes read=input/10, write=input*1.25 when absent) but keep measured self-usage honest: transcripts are dominated by cheap cache reads.

cost.notes: ChatGPT plan — flat-rate marginal cost until usage limits hit

weaknesses: subscription quota is opaque — limits appear without warning
codex.notes: First-party OpenAI harness. Resume supported. soft_weekly_cap is a self-imposed pacing proxy for the plan's invisible usage limits — tune it to your plan; the fleet deprioritizes (not blocks) this provider as delegated usage approaches it.

cost.notes: Free tier: ~20 requests/day — one agentic task can burn several. Paid Antigravity plans raise the cap.

strengths: free tier for occasional mechanical work
weaknesses: no headless session resume — follow-ups need fresh briefs
plain-text output only — no usage/token reporting
tight free-tier daily quota (~20 req/day)
antigravity.notes: Google's Gemini CLI successor (agy >= 1.1.1 required). Headless prints one plain-text response at the end, so no live progress events. Model via --model or ~/.gemini/antigravity-cli/settings.json.

cost.notes: Enterprise Gemini Code Assist licenses only.

weaknesses: RETIRED for free/AI Pro/Ultra accounts — requests stopped serving 2026-06-18
no headless session resume — follow-ups need fresh briefs
gemini.notes: RETIRED 2026-06-18 for free-tier/AI Pro/Ultra accounts; replaced by the Antigravity CLI (see the antigravity entry). Enable this ONLY if you hold an enterprise Gemini Code Assist license, which retains access.

cost.notes: VERIFY current pricing before enabling — this is an example placeholder

weaknesses: weaker multi-step agentic reliability than frontier harnesses
deepseek.notes: Runs through OpenCode. Requires: opencode auth login (deepseek API key).

cost.notes: Local inference — free but occupies the machine

strengths: private — code never leaves the machine
weaknesses: local models fail verification more on multi-step agentic work
slow on consumer hardware
requires LM Studio server running
local-lmstudio.notes: LM Studio via its OpenAI-compatible endpoint, configured as a provider in opencode.json. Set default_model to the exact provider/model name from `opencode models`. restricted trust: only dispatch small, low-blast-radius tasks.

cost.notes: SuperGrok ($30/mo) or X Premium+ ($40/mo) required for grok login; full Grok 4.5 access confirmed only on SuperGrok Heavy as of 2026-07 (lower tiers staged). API pricing if applicable: grok-4.5 $2/$6 per Mtok, grok-build-0.1 $1/$2 — VERIFY before enabling.

strengths: codex-like harness: effort control and session resume
cheap dedicated coding model (grok-build-0.1) for mechanical work
weaknesses: early beta — JSON output schema unpublished, verify parsing on your version
subscription-gated auth
grok.notes: xAI Grok Build CLI (grok -p, --always-approve). Requires: grok login (SuperGrok / X Premium+; --device-auth for headless boxes). First run: verify session id and usage extraction — see the README's verify-before-trusting checklist.

cost.notes: Cursor plan (Pro and up) or CURSOR_API_KEY usage billing — VERIFY your plan's agent quota before enabling.

strengths: mature agent harness with session resume
model choice via -m across frontier vendors
weaknesses: reported to fabricate answers to its own questions in headless mode instead of failing — briefs must be fully self-contained
agent quota on subscription plans is opaque
cursor.notes: Cursor CLI (cursor-agent -p, --force). Auth: cursor-agent login, or CURSOR_API_KEY for headless. context_window depends on the selected model — adjust to your default.

cost.notes: GitHub Copilot subscription; premium-request multipliers vary by model — VERIFY your plan's premium request budget.

strengths: included with a subscription many developers already have
model choice via --model (GPT and Claude families)
weaknesses: plain-text output only — no usage/token reporting
no programmatic session resume — follow-ups need fresh briefs
copilot.notes: GitHub Copilot CLI (copilot -p, --allow-all-tools --no-ask-user). Auth: copilot login or COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN / GITHUB_TOKEN. GitHub recommends containers for --allow-all-tools; the fleet's git-repo-only + diff-review discipline is the mitigation.

cost.notes: PLACEHOLDER — the old Qwen OAuth free tier (~2000 req/day) was discontinued; VERIFY current access (API key or Qwen Coding Plan) and pricing before enabling.

weaknesses: weaker multi-step agentic reliability than frontier harnesses
no sandbox in yolo mode
qwen.notes: Qwen Code CLI (qwen -p, --approval-mode yolo, brief on stdin). Gemini CLI fork with Claude-style stream-json output. Distinct exit codes: 53 = turn limit, 55 = wall-time/tool budget.

cost.notes: PLACEHOLDER — Factory bills by usage and the JSON result reports no token fields; VERIFY billing on your Factory plan before enabling.

strengths: brief passes as a file (-f) — no argv or stdin juggling
session resume and fork; reasoning-effort control
weaknesses: no token usage in JSON output — ledger cost tracking is manual
--auto medium permits git commits; the brief's do-not-commit instruction is the only guard
droid.notes: Factory Droid CLI (droid exec -f, --output-format json, --auto medium via FLEET_DROID_AUTO). Auth: FACTORY_API_KEY. Never raise --auto to high for fleet work (deploy/push territory).

cost.notes: PLACEHOLDER — Amp bills usage-based credits and reports no tokens in execute mode; track spend on the ampcode.com dashboard. VERIFY before enabling.

strengths: no model wrangling — Amp routes models itself
threads sync to ampcode.com for post-hoc inspection
weaknesses: plain-text output — no usage/token reporting
no scriptable resume on current versions — follow-ups need fresh briefs
no model pinning
amp.notes: Amp CLI (amp -x, --dangerously-allow-all). Auth: amp login or AMP_API_KEY. Prefer Amp's settings.json command allowlist over --dangerously-allow-all where possible (set FLEET_AMP_ALLOW_ALL=0 after configuring it). npm: @ampcode/cli.

cost.notes: Claude plan — flat-rate. API-key auth is per_token; claude reports total_cost_usd per run either way.

weaknesses: if the supervisor is Claude Code on the same account, this spends the same quota — parallelism only, not a cost play
claude-worker.notes: Claude Code headless (claude -p). Main uses: non-Claude supervisors (e.g. Codex running fleet) dispatching Claude workers, or a Claude supervisor dispatching haiku for cheap tasks. Resume supported (directory-scoped). review_after: set this to any date a provider's access terms are scheduled to change (e.g. a frontier model moving from subscription tiers to usage credits) — registry.py list flags REVIEW_DUE once it passes, reminding you to re-verify access/cost and update caps.

routing._comment: Cheapest-first cascade the supervisor consults AFTER capability filtering. Order reflects cost: local free -> subscription/free flat -> API per-token. Reorder to taste; the ledger's track record can override this for specific task types.
